## Overview

In Assignment 6 you recognized images with a random forest on raw pixel values. In this assignment you will use the two ideas behind modern image recognition:

-   **Part A, convolutional neural networks (CNNs):** build a CNN in PyTorch, compare it with a fully connected network on Fashion-MNIST, and look inside its first layer.
-   **Part B, transfer learning:** reuse ResNet-18, a large CNN already trained on 1.2 million photos, to recognize **your own categories of images** from only a few dozen examples per category.

## What to Submit

Submit the following on Canvas:

| Deliverable | Format |
|---|---|
| Notebook | The completed `assignment11_student.ipynb`, with all cells run |
| Your images | A zip file of your image folder (or a link to it) |

The easiest way to run the notebook is [Google Colab](https://colab.research.google.com), where PyTorch and torchvision are already installed (upload your image folder to Colab or to Google Drive). On your laptop, install them with `pip install torch torchvision`. Part A takes about 2–4 minutes on a laptop CPU.

## Part A: CNNs on Fashion-MNIST (Questions 1–5)

| Question | Topic |
|---|---|
| 1 | Train a fully connected network (MLP) as a baseline |
| 2 | Build and train a CNN with two convolutional layers |
| 3 | Compare accuracy and parameters; count the parameters of a convolutional layer by hand |
| 4 | Visualize the learned filters and feature maps |
| 5 | Find which classes the CNN confuses with a confusion matrix |

## Part B: Transfer Learning on Your Own Images (Questions 6–8)

1.  Choose **2 to 4 categories** of images you want to recognize, for example dogs vs cats, kinds of food, cars vs trucks, or Bryant buildings.
2.  Collect **at least 30 images per category**. Search engines work well.
3.  Put the images in one folder with **one subfolder per category**:

```
my_images/
    category_1/   img1.jpg, img2.png, ...
    category_2/   ...
```

The notebook reads `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.png`, `.jfif`, `.webp` and `.bmp` files. Images saved from Google are often `.jfif` or `.webp`.

| Question | Topic |
|---|---|
| 6 | Turn every image into 512 features with a pretrained ResNet-18 |
| 7 | Train a classifier on the features; compare it with a random forest on raw pixels |
| 8 | Look at the images the model gets wrong and explain why |

## AI Policy

You may use AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot). Include a short statement describing how you used them and anything they got wrong that you had to fix.
